solution.concept: A quantity with two possible values can lie on either side of a fixed number
solution.explanation: x² − 14x + 48 = (x − 6)(x − 8) = 0, so x = 6 or 8. 6 < 7 but 8 > 7, so no single relation holds.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Quantity I > Quantity II' takes only the larger root.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Quantity I = Quantity II or the relationship cannot be established

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
Compare the two quantities and choose the correct option.
Quantity I: The speed (km/h) of a boat in still water if it goes downstream at 22 km/h and upstream at 14 km/h
Quantity II: The speed (km/h) of a cyclist who covers 50 km in 2 hours 30 minutes

options.text: Quantity I = Quantity II or the relationship cannot be established

solution.concept: Boat speed = (downstream + upstream) ÷ 2; speed = distance ÷ time
solution.explanation: Quantity I = (22 + 14) ÷ 2 = 18 km/h. Quantity II = 50 ÷ 2.5 = 20 km/h. So Quantity I < Quantity II.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Quantity I > Quantity II' uses the downstream speed 22 km/h as the boat's speed.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Quantity I < Quantity II

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
Compare the two quantities and choose the correct option.
Quantity I: Profit percentage when an article is marked 30% above its cost price and sold at a 10% discount
Quantity II: Profit percentage when the cost price of 20 articles equals the selling price of 17 articles

options.text: Quantity I = Quantity II or the relationship cannot be established

solution.concept: Markup–discount profit vs 'cost of n = selling price of m' profit
solution.explanation: Quantity I: 1.3 × 0.9 = 1.17, so 17%. Quantity II: profit = (20 − 17) ÷ 17 = 3/17 ≈ 17.65%. So Quantity I < Quantity II.
steps: II: let CP of 1 article = 1; 17 articles sell for 20
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Quantity I > Quantity II' comes from computing II as 3/20 = 15% (using 20 as the base instead of 17).
solution.final_answer: Option B: Quantity I < Quantity II

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
Compare the two quantities and choose the correct option.
Quantity I: The number of different arrangements of the letters of the word LEVEL
Quantity II: The number of ways of choosing 2 members from a group of 8

options.text: Quantity I = Quantity II or the relationship cannot be established

solution.concept: Arrangements with repeated letters: n! ÷ (p! q!)
solution.explanation: LEVEL has 5 letters with L twice and E twice: 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 120 ÷ 4 = 30. ⁸C₂ = 28. So Quantity I > Quantity II.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Quantity I < Quantity II' comes from dividing 5! by 2! three times (120 ÷ 8 = 15) or from using ⁸P₂ = 56 for Quantity II; a selection of 2 members is unordered, so ⁸C₂ is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Quantity I > Quantity II

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
Compare the two quantities and choose the correct option.
Quantity I: Days taken by A and B together, if A is 50% more efficient than B and B alone takes 30 days
Quantity II: Days taken by C alone, if C and D together take 9 days and D alone takes 18 days

options.text: Quantity I = Quantity II or the relationship cannot be established

solution.concept: Efficiency and time are inversely proportional
solution.explanation: A is 1.5 times as efficient as B, so A alone takes 30 ÷ 1.5 = 20 days and A + B take 1 ÷ (1/20 + 1/30) = 12 days. C's rate = 1/9 − 1/18 = 1/18, so C takes 18 days. So Quantity I < Quantity II.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Quantity I > Quantity II' comes from subtracting days instead of rates for C (18 − 9 = 9 days).
solution.final_answer: Option B: Quantity I < Quantity II

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
Each question below is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer the question.
Question: What is the speed of the train?
I. The train crosses a 200 m long platform in 18 seconds.
II. The train crosses a signal pole in 10 seconds.

options.text: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient
Both statements I and II together are needed
Statements I and II together are not sufficient

solution.concept: Two unknowns (length and speed) need two independent equations
solution.explanation: Statement I gives L + 200 = 18v and statement II gives L = 10v; each has two unknowns. Together, 10v + 200 = 18v, so v = 25 m/s (90 km/h). Both statements are needed.
steps: I alone: L + 200 = 18v — L unknown, not sufficient
II alone: L = 10v — L unknown, not sufficient
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Statement I alone' is tempting because the platform length is known, but the train's own length is not.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Both statements I and II together are needed

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
Each question below is followed by two statements. Decide whether the data in the statements are sufficient to answer the question.
Question: What is the principal deposited by Kavya?
I. The simple interest on it for 3 years at 8% per annum is ₹4,800.
II. The compound interest on it for 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually, is ₹4,200.

options.text: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements I and II together are needed
Either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not

solution.concept: Each statement fixes the rate and time, leaving only the principal unknown
solution.explanation: From I: P = 4,800 × 100 ÷ (8 × 3) = ₹20,000. From II: 0.21P = 4,200, so P = ₹20,000. Each statement alone answers the question.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Both together' is a common choice when one statement looks complicated (compound interest), but II alone has only one unknown.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
The question below is followed by three statements. Decide which statements are sufficient to answer it.
Question: What is Rahul's present age?
I. Rahul is 4 years older than Sita.
II. The ratio of the present ages of Sita and Mohan is 3 : 4.
III. The average present age of Rahul, Sita and Mohan is 28 years.

options.text: Any two of the three statements are sufficient
Only statements I and III together are sufficient
All three statements together are necessary
Even all three statements together are not sufficient

solution.concept: Three unknowns need three independent equations
solution.explanation: There are three unknown ages. I gives R = S + 4, II gives M = 4S/3 and III gives R + S + M = 84. Any two leave one unknown free; all three give S + 4 + S + 4S/3 = 84, so S = 24 and R = 28.
steps: I: R = S + 4; II: M = 4S/3; III: R + S + M = 84
Any two statements: 2 equations, 3 unknowns — not sufficient
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Only I and III' looks enough because III ties all three ages, but without II Mohan's age is free (R + S + M = 84 with R = S + 4 has many solutions).
solution.final_answer: Option C: All three statements together are necessary

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question_text:
The question below is followed by three statements. Decide which statements are sufficient to answer it.
Question: At what rate of interest per annum is a bank lending money?
I. A sum lent at this rate of simple interest doubles itself in 8 years.
II. The simple interest on ₹5,000 for 4 years at this rate is ₹2,500.
III. On ₹16,000 lent for 2 years at this rate, compound interest (compounded annually) exceeds simple interest by ₹250.

options.text: Any one of the three statements alone is sufficient
Either I alone or II alone is sufficient, but III alone is not
Only II and III together are sufficient
All three statements together are necessary

solution.concept: Each statement is a single equation in the rate alone
solution.explanation: I: interest of 100% in 8 years gives R = 12.5%. II: 5,000 × R × 4 ÷ 100 = 2,500 gives R = 12.5%. III: for 2 years, CI − SI = P(R/100)², so 16,000 × (R/100)² = 250, (R/100)² = 1/64 and R = 12.5%. Each statement alone is sufficient.
solution.why_others_wrong: Many reject III alone, not recalling the 2-year formula CI − SI = P(R/100)²; the negative root is impossible for a rate, so III gives a unique answer.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Any one of the three statements alone is sufficient
